correctness.rationale: Ray-circle law of cosines gives the exact truncated-gap coverage. Elementary min inequalities and maximum accessible angular halfwidth prove optimizer equality conditions, including disjoint subcritical packing. Wedge polar integration yields three exact branches. Near tangent regular disks pairwise overlap only with neighbors, and 2-disk lens expansion gives the sharp 3/2 cusp. A second derivative of the radial gap score yields H>0 and quadratic law. Direct numerical polar-integration cross-checks passed, but analytic arguments carry all quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The full 2015 Finch union paper is restricted by its common-origin and remote-center hypotheses; it provides union-area methods but does not establish an all-radius optimizer phase transition or sharp cusp. The 2023 Basit--Langi source treats intersections. The materially inspected full published results on rotated co-centered regular-polygon unions and on circular-center disk intersections are distinguishable by objects and operation, not merely by titles. Neither implies the exact disk-union classification, three area regimes, or stability. A precise unindexed historical predecessor remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Earlier specialized coverage/packing sources could contain an equivalent circular-center union optimization; full historical priority is not certified.
Finch and Tao--Wu supply earlier special-case disk-union area identities; do not claim those identities as new.
Generic angular arc truncation is classical; the originality claim is the combined exact critical optimizer/stability phase diagram.

value.rationale: The natural constraint of equal sensor disks fixed to a circle undergoes exact nonunique-to-rigid optimization at first contact. The three closed area regimes, all-optimizer classification, and change of the loss exponent from flat to 3/2 to quadratic quantify genuinely distinct geometric sensitivity near tangency. The explicit parallel-body gap also measures loss of convexification at large radii.
